mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a period of economic expansion signals an anticipatory monetary easing, which lowers long-term interest rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in real personal income (not directly available, but proxied by combined growth in GDPC1 and PAYEMS) above 0.5% coincides with a rise in consumer spending, boosting corporate revenues and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and PAYEMS both show > 0.5% month-over-month growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
